overall_reason: A deploy list whose status icons come from three different kits, so the card has no single visual system.

score.reason: T-OWN-SYSTEM and T-MIRROR fail: a purple gradient tile, an orange filled circle and a pink square with a red triangle sit in one list, plus a teal check inside the Deploy button.

findings.evidence: 'Checkout redesign' has a purple gradient tile with a white check, 'Search speedup' an orange filled circle with a refresh glyph, 'Pricing copy' a pink square with a red triangle, and the 'Deploy' button a teal check badge.
findings.before: Four icon treatments from different sets
findings.after: One icon set in one style, with colour used only for deploy state
findings.why: Mixed kits make the card read as assembled from parts, not drawn by one hand.

findings.evidence: The icon shapes (check, refresh, triangle) carry state, but their loud fills (purple, orange, pink) carry nothing, so the colour competes with the deploy names.
findings.before: Decorative colour fills on every status
findings.after: Neutral list with state in a small, consistent mark
findings.why: On an Operate screen the deploy names and their state are the task; decoration pulls the eye away.

strengths: The content structure (name, branch and author, relative time, one Deploy action) fits the job.
not_investigated: 00-contract.md is absent: no brand authority, audience or overrides were available, so the item was read as an Operate composition (CON-018).
T-RIVAL-NAME cap: the composition names no client, so every placeholder label holds under any rival; the cap at 5 was not applied and the test was used only to spot default copy.
T-IDEA-CARRIES: single composition, there is no second screen to carry the idea.
T-DELETE-PICTURE and T-PROMISE-PICTURED: no lead image and no marketing promise, except where a finding says so.
T-COVER-TEXT: no brand theme or motif to recognise.
The caption above some frames ('Considered composition' / 'Composition problem') is fixture text from the capture host and was not judged.
